A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOTS research and contain 18 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical substantive content, with differences confined to publication headers and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original DOTS benchmark evaluations, ablations, efficiency and trajectory analyses, and appendix case studies and BBH subtask results.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains the same original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 3–5, ablations in Table 6, and appendix results in Table 10.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same atomic reasoning actions, iterative trajectory search in Algorithm 1, and external and internalized planner training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MATH, BBH, Game of 24, TheoremQA, DeepMind Math, MMLU-pro, StrategyQA, and DROP. The in-distribution, few-shot, OOD, and few-shot in-context evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain identical comparator membership, including CoT, PoT, LTM, PromptAgent, Self-refine, and Vanilla SFT where originally evaluated. Appendix B's GPT-4o comparisons and Table 10's CoT/PoT comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1 and 3.8 and Appendix A retain identical data selections, sample counts, model configurations, answer-scoring procedures, zero-shot and few-shot prompting settings, and training hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The search and explanation ablations, OOD evaluation, action-distribution analysis, efficiency and difficulty analyses, and Appendix B case studies are identical. Appendix C retains the same BBH error analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain four evaluations per candidate during trajectory search in Appendix A. Benchmark uncertainty reporting is unchanged; neither reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative outcomes in Tables 3–10, Figure 3, and the appendix cases are identical. For example, Table 3 retains external-planner MATH accuracies of 57.7% with Llama-3-70B-Instruct and 75.4% with GPT-4o-mini.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the trajectory-search mathematical formulation and cost reasoning, and the trajectory-length definition are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about dynamic reasoning-action selection, the two planner paradigms, performance relative to static methods, and allocating more reasoning steps to harder problems.

C2.justification: Interpretations of task and solver adaptation, joint planner/solver optimization, and computational efficiency are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same explanation of date-understanding failures caused by program output-format errors.

D1.justification: Appendix A's search settings, training-example counts, LitGPT implementation, and fine-tuning hyperparameters are identical. Appendix D's prompts and the stated code-access link are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list, and Section 4 positioning are identical, including distinctions from static prompt optimization and search over individual CoT reasoning steps.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'. The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 4 October 2024 to v2 dated 7 August 2025. Body wording and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, Tables 1–10, captions, algorithm and appendix boxes, and their placement are identical. Header and arXiv-stamp wording changes do not alter the body layout.

improvement.justification: The substantive text, experimental evidence, mathematical content, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are identical. The updated publication header and arXiv stamp document publication status without meaningfully changing scientific support, clarity, or reproducibility.
